criteria.title: Numerator & Denominator Meaning
criteria.description: Explains that the denominator tells the total number of equal parts and numerator counts the parts considered.

levels.demonstrated: Clearly identifies both numerator (count of selected pieces) and denominator (total equal parts dividing the whole).
levels.partial: Mentions one component correctly or confuses top and bottom slightly.
levels.incorrect: Gives an erroneous definition (e.g. claims denominator is just an extra number).
levels.not_demonstrated: Does not discuss what numerator or denominator mean.

criteria.title: Equal-Sized Parts Requirement
criteria.description: Explains that parts of the whole must be identical in size (fair shares).

levels.demonstrated: Explicitly emphasizes that pieces must be of equal size or fair shares.
levels.partial: Implies equality without clearly stating it as a requirement.
levels.incorrect: Claims parts can be any random size without affecting fraction names.

criteria.title: Partition Count vs Part Size Relationship
criteria.description: Understands that dividing a whole into more parts results in smaller individual parts.

levels.demonstrated: Clearly states that dividing a whole into more pieces makes each piece smaller (e.g. 1/5 is smaller than 1/3).
levels.partial: Understands that denominators change part size but expresses the direction hesitantly.
levels.incorrect: Claims cutting into more pieces makes each piece bigger (reversed rule).
levels.not_demonstrated: Does not mention the relationship between number of parts and part size.

criteria.title: Valid Comparison Method
criteria.description: Compares fractions using a mathematically sound method (equal numerators, equal denominators, common denominators, or visual benchmark).

levels.demonstrated: Applies a valid comparison method (e.g. same numerator reasoning, common denominator, or visual strips).
levels.partial: Compares fractions correctly but explanation of why the method works is incomplete.
levels.incorrect: Uses whole-number bias or compares numerators only while ignoring denominators.
levels.not_demonstrated: Does not demonstrate any fraction comparison method.

criteria.title: Equivalent Fractions Concept
criteria.description: Explains that equivalent fractions have equal value and are formed by multiplying/dividing by the same factor (not adding).

levels.demonstrated: Explains that equivalent fractions represent the same quantity and are created by multiplying or dividing numerator and denominator by the same number.
levels.partial: Recognizes equivalent fractions by example (e.g. 1/2 = 2/4) without explaining proportional scaling.
levels.incorrect: Claims that adding the same number to top and bottom keeps fractions equivalent.
